findings.reason: The excerpt quotes Amendment I as stating that Congress shall make no law abridging freedom of speech.

evidence.text:
The National Archives identifies this as a transcription of the enrolled original; its spelling and punctuation reflect the original. Congress proposed 12 amendments on September 25, 1789; ten were ratified on December 15, 1791, forming the Bill of Rights. Article 2 was ratified in 1992 as the 27th Amendment; Article 1 was never ratified. The page was last reviewed August 7, 2025.

Amendment I: Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

findings.claim: The First Amendment requires Congress to license every newspaper before publication.
findings.reason: The quoted text says Congress shall make no law abridging freedom of speech or of the press; it does not require Congress to license newspapers, and that claimed mandate conflicts with the quoted prohibition.
